thread:
arthur: kicking off a canary traffic shift to gpu-pool-eu, automation started but it failed midway. canary replicas getting evicted and autoscaler didn't add nodes. anyone seeing this?

deepa: on it. which pipeline did the shift use? gitops or manual?
arthur: gitops -> progressive-delivery/splitter applied by argo at 12:05 UTC. automation log shows 'apply succeeded' but traffic only moved to ~35% then errors.

mike: I see errors in the cluster events: some pods in canary group were OOMKilled then evicted with scheduling failure: Insufficient cpu/gpu and NodeAffinity mismatch. also kube-autoscaler logs show API permission denied to read node-pool tags. posting snippets: 

```
kubectl get events -n inference -o wide | tail -n 10
2026-02-15T12:06:02Z Pod gpu-canary-7ddb Evicted FailedScheduling No nodes available for requested gpu type
2026-02-15T12:06:04Z Pod gpu-canary-7ddb Killed OOMKilled Memory usage spiked 12Gi > limit 8Gi
```

and autoscaler: 

```
I0215 12:07:10 autoscaler.go:342] unable to list nodepools: permission denied (403) on compute.nodePools.get
```

infra-bot: alert: gitops-apply: progressive-delivery/splitter -> partial traffic applied (35%). Fallback policy not triggered. See runbook: https://intranet.runbooks/redwood/prog-delivery

arthur: also noticed a networkpolicy change in the last terraform apply that blocks kube-system -> node-provisioner endpoints. could that stop autoscaler health checks?

mike: yep, terraform drift—recent workspace update renamed the nodepool label key from "redwood:gpu=rtx6000" to "redwood:gpu=rtx6000:legacy" (bad). autoscaler looks for nodes with label selector `redwood/gpu` and got 0 matches. planning diff: 

```
- labels = { "redwood:gpu" = "rtx6000" }
+ labels = { "redwood:gpu:legacy" = "rtx6000" }
```

jen: can we revert the label change or update autoscaler selector? which is safer right now?

deepa: quick fix = revert terraform workspace to previous commit that had correct labels, run terraform apply for nodepool labels only. medium = patch autoscaler to accept both label keys. long = reconcile pipeline to validate nodepool labels pre-apply.

sre-bot: automated action: progressive-delivery/fallback detected instability, initiating rollback to previous traffic split at 12:13 UTC. rollback status: in_progress

arthur: patching networkpolicy to allow control plane -> node-provisioner temporarily so autoscaler can query nodepools. executing: 

```bash
kubectl patch networkpolicy allow-controlplane -n infra --patch '{"spec":{"podSelector":{},"ingress":[{"from":[{"namespaceSelector":{"matchLabels":{"kubernetes.io/metadata.name":"kube-system"}}}]}]}}'
```

mike: after patch, autoscaler logs show it can list nodepools but still 0 matched due to label drift. planning to run terraform rollback now.

arthur: applying rollback terraform plan for nodepool labels (targeting module.gke.node_pools[1]). running `terraform apply -target=module.gke.node_pools[1]`

infra-bot: terraform apply finished: nodepool labels restored. cloud events: new nodes registered (2 rtx6000 nodes).

arthur: canary traffic resumed to 20% then 50% successfully. monitoring metrics: p95 latency up 10ms, token cost roughly stable.

deepa: quick cost check — if we instead increased reserved burst capacity to avoid future autoscale delays, estimate ~+$8k/mo based on current utilization. not trivial but manageable for critical eu workloads.

jen: next steps: 1) add a pre-apply gitops check to validate nodepool label keys 2) add an automated test for networkpolicy impact on autoscaler 3) create runbook to prefer label fix over autoscaler selector change.

mike: filed infra ticket: INFRA-478: prevent label-key renames in terraform workspace; added a guard in PR template.

arthur: marking this thread resolved for now. rollback succeeded and canary completed after manual fix. leaving follow-up items in INFRA-478 and progressive-delivery runbook update. thanks y'all :thumbsup:

sre-bot: incident summary generated: https://incidents.redwood/2026-02-15-canary-drift-1768501234 (draft)
